reading.body:
This record is a small wireless internet provider's equipment site in Aulla, Italy, not a commercial data center, and it carries no published power capacity.

The entry comes from OpenStreetMap, where a node is tagged telecom=data_center and named Wi-Fi Communication Aulla. The name points to a fixed-wireless internet or communications business, the kind that serves rural and hilly parts of Italy where wired broadband is thin. A site like this would be a base station or network operations point handling backhaul and management for a regional wireless network. That is real telecom infrastructure, but it is a different business and a different scale from a colocation facility renting space to outside customers.

For AI specifically, the record says almost nothing. The power field is zero, which here means no capacity was recorded, not that the site draws no electricity. There is no operator listed, no confirmation against a company website, and the research status is exhausted, so the classification rests on a name and a tag rather than verified business records. A wireless ISP's equipment site does not host training clusters or serve as a grid-scale load.

What the data does not cover is the part that would matter for any compute argument: actual power draw, building footprint, cooling, or whether the site does anything beyond routing wireless traffic. It also does not establish that this is a data center at all. The honest reading is a single unconfirmed point on a map, useful as an example of how loosely the data-center label gets applied, and not usable as evidence about AI infrastructure.
